title: Why Sewer Gas Smells Escape Into Buildings
description: Sewer gas entering a living space is frequently caused by a failure in the trap seal or inadequate drainage venting. Every plumbing fixture requires a trap containing water to block hazardous gases. When a fixture sits unused, the standing water inside the trap can evaporate over time. Additionally, improper venting causes pressure imbalances that siphon water out of traps when nearby fixtures drain. Plumbers must verify that water seals remain intact and vents are clear to prevent foul odors, health hazards, and pressure problems in residential drainage systems.

Why Sewer Gas Smells Escape Into Buildings

Sewer gas entering a living space is frequently caused by a failure in the trap seal or inadequate drainage venting. Every plumbing fixture requires a trap containing water to block hazardous gases. When a fixture sits unused, the standing water inside the trap can evaporate over time. Additionally, improper venting causes pressure imbalances that siphon water out of traps when nearby fixtures drain. Plumbers must verify that water seals remain intact and vents are clear to prevent foul odors, health hazards, and pressure problems in residential drainage systems.
